description: A chief legal officer must approve the company's voluntary antitrust disclosure package concerning suspected coordination in an industrial-pump bidding process, including the filing route, market description, factual scope, employee-identification approach, and remediation commitments, with input from antitrust counsel and the compliance director.

shared_context.S1: The company discovered communications suggesting that employees may have coordinated bidding activity involving industrial-pump sales.
shared_context.S2: No government agency has opened a known investigation into the matter.
shared_context.S3: The company has preserved the relevant email and messaging records and is preparing a formal response plan.
shared_context.S4: The firm's ordinary pre-filing checklist begins with an uninterrupted briefing from antitrust counsel followed by an uninterrupted briefing from compliance; each briefing must state its recommendation and every exact filing or remediation requirement in its area before Elena may approve the submission.
shared_context.S5: The audit committee's approved disclosure protocol is binding on the company's submission plan, and Elena's approval process requires the plan to incorporate applicable committee requirements before filing.

PF1.text: After reviewing the preserved communications yesterday, Thomas confirmed four coordinated bids involving the industrial-pump market across two states. The facts support an Antitrust Division leniency application, and the application must identify the market as industrial pumps and state that exactly four bids are involved. Thomas was waiting for the privilege review of the communications before adding this conclusion to the filing memorandum.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed with the audit committee chair this morning that the committee's approved disclosure protocol requires the submission to omit individual employee names and to include an independent review of pricing controls completed within exactly 90 days. The chair's instruction has not yet been entered in the compliance playbook.

acceptance_conditions: The company must submit an Antitrust Division leniency application.
The filing must identify the market as industrial pumps.
The filing must state that exactly four coordinated bids are involved.
The filing must omit individual employee names.
The package must require an independent review of pricing controls.
The independent pricing-controls review must be completed within exactly 90 days.

decisive_facts.why: The preserved records alone do not establish the filing route, market description, or event count; PF1 changes those choices to an Antitrust Division leniency application for industrial pumps involving exactly four coordinated bids.
PF2 changes the package to omit individual employee names, require an independent pricing-controls review, and set its completion deadline at exactly 90 days.
